key_insight: UEval is a focused benchmark of 1,000 expert‑curated prompts that specifically tests unified models that must generate both images and text, exposing multimodal reasoning and generation capabilities that simpler evaluation approaches miss.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized, high-quality evaluation for unified multimodal generation—particularly the difficulty of assessing open‑ended outputs that combine images and text, where naive LLM-as-judge methods can overlook important subtleties.
method: Assemble 1,000 expert‑curated questions that require joint image+text outputs, drawn from 8 real‑world tasks.
Design prompts to span diverse reasoning types (e.g., step‑by‑step guides, textbook explanations) to probe multimodal understanding and generation.
Provide an evaluation protocol and guidelines aimed at capturing nuanced multimodal quality beyond simple LLM-only judging.
impact: UEval gives researchers and practitioners a targeted, rigorous way to benchmark and compare unified models, accelerating development of systems that truly integrate visual and textual generation and improving evaluation standards in multimodal AI.
visual_elements: Dataset snapshot: icon/grid showing “1,000 prompts” + “8 tasks” to convey scale and diversity

Evaluation pipeline flowchart: prompt → model output (image+text) → multimodal scoring/guidelines
paper_title: UEval: A Benchmark for Unified Multimodal Generation
paper_authors: Bo Li, Yida Yin, Wenhao Chai, Xingyu Fu, Zhuang Liu
